solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soldiers reportedly capture Scotsman's province overseas

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service regiment

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for capture is to be heard rather than seen spelt

parts.note: to capture is to catch
Ewan is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Special forces are said to have seized a Scot's homeland abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns CATCH into KATCH, which sounds the same. The possessive on 'Scotsman's' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saskatchewan is one of Canada's prairie provinces, so it is a province across the ocean from Britain.

clue.text: Month after month one's put up with Sweden's programmes

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up reads its letters from bottom to top
after places one month's letters following the other's

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October, a month
one is I, and one's stands for one is, giving I plus S
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Month after month someone tolerates Swedish television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses MOCTIS, built from the months and one's, to SITCOM; Sweden's S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitcoms are situation comedies, a kind of television programme.

clue.text: Source of message about learner driver's fine

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other

parts.note: the sender of a message is where it comes from
L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A text informs a learner that they have been fined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty but is the adjective meaning thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine as in a fine thread is a synonym of thin and narrow.

clue.text: Relate badly and upset extremely good confidants

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the preceding word are disordered
in a down clue, upset means turned over, so these letters read upwards

parts.note: so can mean extremely, as in so kind

explanation.surface: Getting on poorly with others and being terribly upset by good friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges RELATE to ALTERE; 'upset' turns SOG into GOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A close trusted friend can be called a second self, a partner one confides in.

clue.text: One's sometimes pulled in to beach child's play — I must be old

definitions.text: One's sometimes pulled in to beach

indicators.note: must be says one letter is to be replaced by another in the word just named

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy, like child's play
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at the seaside shrugs that beach games make them feel old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I must be old' tells you to swap the I in CINCH for O.
explanation.definitionFit: A large spiral seashell is often hauled ashore by fishermen or carried in by the tide to the sand.

clue.text: Missing one part, exhibit originally under sea brought to surface

indicators.note: missing means the named letters are taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
a bit is a part of something

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A museum piece missing a section is recovered from the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' removes I and BIT from EXHIBIT, leaving EXH.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhumed means dug up from the ground, brought up into the open.

clue.text: With note for installation, alarm kit

indicators.note: for installation says one piece is fitted inside the other

parts.note: to alarm is to appal
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A burglar alarm kit comes with a note on how to install it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit can mean clothing or gear, and apparel is clothing.

clue.text: Secretive types turned up gold, mostly testing in faults

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: sins are faults or wrongdoings

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: crucial can mean severely testing, as in a crucial trial

explanation.surface: Prospectors found gold, though most of their tests were flawed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses gold in a down clue; 'mostly' trims the testing word by one letter before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosicrucians belong to an esoteric brotherhood famed for its secret teachings.

clue.text: Secretly not shocked, base infiltrated by English close to midnight

indicators.note: shocked hair is tousled, so the word before it is scrambled
infiltrated by means the next piece slips inside the base

parts.note: HQ, headquarters, is a military base

indicators.note: close to points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Unfazed, a soldier notes an English spy slipped into base just before midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocked' rearranges NOT to ONT. QT is short for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for doing something quietly means secretly, without others knowing.

clue.text: Two stage productions nearly a failure

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is left off

parts.note: Noh is Japanese masked drama and opera is sung drama, two kinds of stage production

explanation.surface: Putting on two shows almost ended in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no hope of success is a failure, in informal usage.

clue.text: Composer's note in arrangement for harmonica — fortissimo

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as the composer is

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
an arrangement rearranges the music, so the word that follows is reordered

parts.note: ff is the musical marking for fortissimo, very loud

explanation.surface: A composer's piece is scored for harmonica, to be played very loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement for' scrambles HARMONICA, with N placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Rachmaninoff was a Russian composer and pianist.

clue.text: Wearing pattern that's appropriate

parts.note: in means wearing, as in in uniform
an order is an arrangement or pattern

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a patterned outfit is suitable to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acceptable or fitting in the circumstances is in order.

clue.text: One in church on seat of old poet

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts this piece after the one it sits on

parts.note: a seat can mean a home, as in a country seat

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: RC stands for the Roman Catholic church
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone in a church pew sits on the seat once used by an old poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer was the ancient Greek epic poet, and the adjective describes things relating to him.

clue.text: Upright piano scratched from lever meeting resistance

indicators.note: scratched from means the named letter is struck out of the word

parts.note: a prise is a lever, something to prise with
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An upright piano is withdrawn from a lever mechanism under resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical part of a stair, the upright between treads.

clue.text: Flash around cash for foreigner's ambitious contract

indicators.note: around means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: flash, as in showy, can mean glam
the rand is South Africa's currency, a foreigner's cash

explanation.surface: A flashy dealer surrounds money for an overseas client's big deal.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, the contract to win all thirteen tricks is the most ambitious bid.

clue.text: Countermand an admirer hugging large people

indicators.note: hugging means the first piece wraps around the next ones

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fan
men can mean people, as in all men

explanation.surface: An admirer is told to stop embracing so many people.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a countermand is a revocation of an order, a cancellation.

clue.text: Article on imperialist acquiring posh lover

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the article after the imperialist
acquiring means taking another piece inside

parts.note: Hernan Cortes was the Spanish conquistador who took Mexico for the empire
U means upper-class, posh
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A conquistador takes up with an upper-class mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a kept mistress of rich or noble men.

clue.text: Ignorant Frenchman's one with sore over in A&E

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: taken as its letters A and E

indicators.note: over means the word is turned round

parts.note: a raw wound is sore

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with a sore turns up at the emergency department, clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital accident and emergency department; 'over' reverses RAW to WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ignorant of something is not knowing about it, a synonym of oblivious.

clue.text: One supporting ruler's flowing garments in case of torrent

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as one supporting a ruler is

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the case of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: saris are long flowing garments worn by South Asian women

explanation.surface: A monarch's flowing robes are caught in a torrent.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the Russian emperor and autocratic rule was a tsarist.

clue.text: Layer on skirt of Angus for pasty

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the layer after the skirt
the skirt of something is its edge, here the word's outer letters

parts.note: a hen is a layer, as it lays eggs

explanation.surface: A Scotsman in a kilt with layers on, looking pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' is not a stratum but one that lays: a hen. Angus is a Scottish name and region.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty skin is pale and unhealthy-looking, as is a grey, drained face.

clue.text: Player's heart is tested to some extent

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as the player is

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sportsman's courage is put to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a performer, such as an entertainer playing on stage.

clue.text: Loathsome hot woolly is one stifling uniform

indicators.note: stifling means smothering another piece inside
woolly means muddled, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hot woolly jumper is unpleasant to wear with a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' scrambles IS ONE, which holds the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heinous is wicked, odious and detestable.

clue.text: Regularly ignored tapioca on a sheep's tongue

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the tapioca letters after the sheep

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Tapioca is routinely left uneaten on a sheep's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' looks like part of the sheep but is the definition: a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic language, and tongue means a language.

clue.text: Sound collective noun — origin of genealogists?

parts.note: a clan is a family group, a collective term for kin

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a collective noun is sound and whether genealogists coined it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic noise.

clue.text: European set on a piercing to stud back

indicators.note: piercing means pushing through, so these letters go inside the reversed stud
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nail is a stud, as on a boot

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the set after the a

parts.note: a TV is a set, a television set

explanation.surface: A fashion piece: a set of piercings fitted with a stud at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives LIAN; 'European' here is a person, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Latvia, a Baltic state, is a European.

clue.text: Vigour gives life to non-European revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters are reversed
non-European means the abbreviation for European is removed

parts.note: to animate something is to give it life

explanation.surface: A non-European revolutionary's vigour inspires life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-European' drops E from ANIMATES to ANIMATS; 'revolutionary' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, physical energy and endurance.

clue.text: Aged fellow on stand, not the last to relent

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the aged fellow after the stand
not the last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting
of can mean aged, as in a man of eighty

explanation.surface: An old man on the stand, not the final witness, finally relents.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to slacken off or become less severe, an idiom for letting up.

clue.text: Follow street and go round the bend to keep hospital engagements

parts.note: to get something is to follow or understand it

indicators.note: to keep means the scrambled letters hold another inside
round the bend means crazy, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Follow the street and drive round the bend to reach the hospital appointments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' gives TOGETERS, which 'to keep' wraps around the hospital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherings and parties are social engagements, informal meetings of people.
